instruction: Browse men's short-sleeve shirts on the Macy's website.

metadata.trajectory_summary: Agent navigated from macys.com homepage to Men's Shirts section, applied Short Sleeve and Size L filters, but failed to find and apply the 50% discount filter. Spent remaining turns cycling through Price dropdown (dollar ranges only), Filter sidebar, and product detail pages without finding the discount option.
metadata.capability_extraction: Can navigate macys.com category hierarchy (Men > Clothing > Shirts), apply sleeve length filter (Short Sleeve), apply size filter (L, Men's Regular), open filter panels and dropdowns, click products and navigate back
metadata.failure_analysis: Model could not locate the discount percentage filter. The Price dropdown only showed dollar ranges ($50, $50-100, etc.), not percentage off options. Model kept cycling through available filters without finding the correct one, exhausting all 50 turns.
metadata.task_rationale: Decomposed original task to single-filter sub-task: navigate to shirts and apply short sleeve filter. Model clearly demonstrated this capability by screenshot 5-10.
metadata.explanation: Task requires navigating to men's shirts and applying the short sleeve filter. Evaluator checks URL contains both men's shirts path and Short Sleeve filter parameter.

llm_judge_reasons: Getter 'active_url_from_accessTree' correctly extracts the active Chrome tab URL from the accessibility tree and returns a string, which the metric can consume.

Metric 'is_expected_url_pattern_match' correctly receives the rules dict (after get_rule unwraps it) and accesses rules['expected'] to get the pattern list. Each pattern is checked via re.search against the URL.
Pattern 'macys\.com.*mens.*shirts' reasonably verifies navigation to the men's shirts section on Macy's.
Pattern 'Short.*Sleeve' verifies the short sleeve filter is applied, matching URL parameters like 'Short+Sleeve' or 'Short%20Sleeve'.
Both instruction requirements (men's shirts + short sleeve filter) are covered by the two regex patterns.

Minor concern: Both regex patterns are case-sensitive. Macy's URLs may use varying casing (e.g., 'short+sleeve' lowercase) which would cause a false negative. Using case-insensitive patterns (e.g., '(?i)Short.*Sleeve') would be more robust.
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Consider making regex patterns case-insensitive by prepending (?i) to each pattern, e.g., '(?i)macys\.com.*mens.*shirts' and '(?i)Short.*Sleeve', to handle URL casing variations on Macy's website.
